spec_conformance_summary: The main responsibility split follows M1-M4: no Rust PBS enumeration/version table or custom dependency solver remains; uv receives the exact dependency request without optional extras or source builds, and incompatibility fails before admission without interpreter fallback. Reuse precedes live resolution, excludes uv executable availability from environment identity, and validates recorded interpreter/distribution observations. Schema-1 plans and legacy release flags are explicitly rejected with migration guidance, as permitted by M3. Stable private base/cache directories are not moved or swept; preparation and fixed-path publication retain their ownership/failure boundaries. CLI/resident/protocol/pool/supervisor files and Cargo.lock are unchanged. Acceptance nevertheless fails for the compile regression, the newly introduced post-publication root-inference defect, and removal of unrelated transfer-safety assertions described below. uv 0.11.29 version/help inspection confirms the composed command options exist; it is not live environment evidence. No source/spec fixes, subagents, Git delivery actions, heavyweight Rust gates, Docker execution or runtime provisioning were performed.
test_assertion_review: Read the complete changed installer unit/integration assertions and new fixture/probe/smoke files. Removing PBS enumeration, tar extraction and Rust PyPI metadata-selection assertions is justified by M1/M3; replacing PBS archive corruption with retained-wheel corruption, fixed site-packages spelling with probed venv paths, and ordinary-only snapshots with symlink-target-aware snapshots reflects the new ownership model. Fixed-path replacement, old-only sentinel removal, no-fetch byte-identical reuse, failed-preparation snapshots, manifest/worker/binary hashes, foreign-staging preservation, native locks/permissions, uncertain-writer preservation and post-rename cleanup disarming remain asserted. The new command-injection test checks delegation rather than claiming real uv behavior. F3 identifies the unrelated binary-transfer assertion loss. F1 currently prevents native integration-test compilation. Independently ran only the four mocked tests in scripts/tests/test_runtime_boot_smoke.py with python -B: 4 passed in 0.003 seconds; they confirm argument/exit handling, not container boot. A tiny AST-extracted check of worker/probe_environment.py:32 reproduced F2 for both PurePosixPath and PureWindowsPath without files, subprocess provisioning or environment installation. Windows/Linux Rust tests, actual uv publication/relocation, release builds, containment/onefile tests and real upstream boot remain pending CI.

blocking_findings.description: [P2] Do not infer the installation root from its basename. worker/probe_environment.py:32 treats any root whose parent is named staging as a candidate. With the supported --libs-dir /downloads/staging and the default managed interpreter under /downloads/staging/uv-python, candidate root /downloads/staging/staging/runtime-<id> correctly infers /downloads/staging and passes. After rename, root /downloads/staging/runtime incorrectly infers /downloads; line 33 then forbids the entire /downloads/staging tree and rejects the valid stable base. Thus every managed boot using a private root named staging fails only after publication, and a replacement can already have retired the old runtime at src/runtime_installer.rs:1580. Subsequent startups repeat the failure. The same path calculation reproduces with C:/libs/staging. I executed the actual AST-extracted lines 32-35 with both path flavors: candidate PASS, published FAIL ('base interpreter is inside replaceable storage'). No contract forbids this libs-dir basename.
